correctness.rationale: Expansion under the split Segre parametrization gives the bidegree-(3,3) equation f(s)f(t)=kappa. In characteristic two f′(T)=T²: for κ≠0, affine singularities force s=t=0 and κ=1, while boundary infinity points are smooth since zeros of f are simple. κ=0 is reducible/singular, κ=1 has a singular point. Connectedness follows from H¹(O(-3,-3))=0; adjunction gives genus four and the canonical embedding. Nonsplit quadric forbids ground-field degree-three maps; the rational point [1:t²:t:0] gives degree ≤4 by Riemann–Roch. The t-count proof covers every 2^m≥4. The exact symbolic Segre identity and finite-field gradient computations in verify.py replay successfully.

value.rationale: A single explicit family simultaneously gives the exact smoothness discriminant of a canonical (2,3) pencil in characteristic two and a uniform rational-point selection proving gonality exactly four over every even finite field of size at least four. This addresses a natural genus-four case of Faber–Grantham–Howe’s minimum/maximum gonality existence question without just extending a finite census, and distinguishes ground-field from geometric gonality. The prior F_2 construction does not subsume these infinitely many characteristic-two base fields.
